title: Thursday's boring SaaS, 15 October 2026
dek: Thursday, 15 October 2026. Ten are Stripe-verified. Wawp's number also includes Dodo. Email Hackers' Stripe key expired in May.

companies.name: Tailride
companies.description: Finds invoices in an accountant's inbox in seconds (company-stated). TrustMRR positions it as AI accounting automation for tax filings and invoice management, aimed at accountants managing multiple clients. Pricing (company-stated): free for 10 invoices a month, then $19 for 75 invoices a month. Founded Oct 2024 in Spain.
companies.evidence: All-time ~$119,345, last 12 months ~$87,263, last 6 months ~$628, last 3 months $0, last 30 days $0. MRR snapshot ~$34, 1 active subscription. Revenue cliff after a strong last 12 months. Do not read all-time as the current run-rate. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~10:04 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Pick one painful accountant workflow (inbox invoices, bank PDF to ledger, VAT pack) in one country and charge per client or per document pack.
companies.whyItPrints: Accountants live in email. A tool that pulls invoices out of the inbox and into the tax workflow is legacy process glue. The all-time Stripe total shows the niche can pay. The collapsed current monthly figure is the cautionary half of the story.

companies.name: Local SEO Bot
companies.description: Dashboard to help small and medium local businesses show up on Google Maps: automate listings, track rankings, get more calls (company-stated). Pricing from $99 a month, cancel anytime, 30-day money-back (company-stated). ~535 users (founder-stated). Founded Apr 2025, US.
companies.evidence: ~$11,666 MRR, 82 active subscriptions, ~$12,417 L30 (+5.3%), ~$33,987 last 3 months, ~$54,332 last 6 months, ~$92,497 last 12 months, ~$102,812 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~04:18 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One local vertical (dentists, roofers, HVAC) plus Maps ranking and review ops. Charge a monthly fee and skip the AI pitch.
companies.whyItPrints: Local owners pay monthly to show up on Maps. Same play as directories and rank trackers, sold as done-for-you work.

companies.name: Email Hackers
companies.description: Brazilian company that sells email-marketing management software to the local market as an ActiveCampaign reseller (founder-stated description on TrustMRR). Founded Oct 2023, Brazil.
companies.evidence: MRR snapshot ~$7,241, 122 active subscriptions, ~$6,841 L30, ~$6,782 last 6 months, ~$45,264 last 12 months, ~$418,952 all-time. Last synced 15 May 2026 ~14:40 Warsaw. The Stripe API key expired, so these figures are a May 2026 snapshot, not live October data.
companies.indieAngle: Become the local reseller and onboarding partner for one proven product in one country that hates US billing and English support.
companies.whyItPrints: A country-specific reseller and implementation layer on a global email platform. Package it, bill locally, and support Brazilian small businesses.

companies.name: ZebraSnap
companies.description: Marketplace where sports photographers sell photos to the athletes in them. Buyers find themselves with a selfie, a bib number, or a shirt-color search (company-stated). Commission runs from 16% down to 5% by plan, plus photographer subscriptions at Lite $16.99 a month and Pro $29.99 a month (company-stated). Founded Jul 2024, US.
companies.evidence: ~$31,347 L30 (+34.9%), ~$73,900 last 3 months, ~$117,136 last 6 months, last 12 months and all-time ~$144,753. MRR snapshot ~$766, 24 active subscriptions. Most cash is marketplace take-rate, not seats. L30 profit margin 75% (TrustMRR snapshot). Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~07:11 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One sport and one region. Sell the photos, not the seats.
companies.whyItPrints: A two-sided event-media take-rate business. Photographers upload, athletes pay for their shots, the platform skims. No enterprise sales cycle.

companies.name: Refined Listings
companies.description: Virtual staging and marketing toolkit for real estate agents and property managers: MLS import, multi-angle staging, a style catalog, object removal, and photo-to-video (company-stated). The founder says they did $800k+ lifetime as an agency, then moved to software in Oct 2025. Pricing is pay-as-you-go credit packs from $128 to $750, with about an 18% repeat purchase rate (company-stated). ~3,500 users (founder-stated). Listed for sale at $495,000, about 1.4× (TrustMRR).
companies.evidence: ~$29,357 L30 (−23.5%), ~$94,669 last 3 months, ~$149,539 last 6 months, ~$232,667 last 12 months, ~$266,829 all-time. MRR snapshot ~$752, 8 active subscriptions. Credit packs dominate over a classic monthly seat figure. L30 profit margin 68% (TrustMRR snapshot). Asking price $495,000. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~07:17 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Credits, not seats, for one realtor workflow (staging, floor plans, listing video). Sell packs.
companies.whyItPrints: Agents need listing photos that sell. Credits beat seats when usage is bursty. A clear buyer and a sale listing.

companies.name: StudyScout
companies.description: Aggregates high-paying online studies and focus groups. The founder claims no paid ads, fully organic, viral short-video growth (founder-stated). Founded Jan 2026, US. Listed for sale at $70,000, about 1.1× (TrustMRR). L30 profit margin 69% (TrustMRR snapshot).
companies.evidence: ~$5,174 MRR, 694 active subscriptions, ~$5,274 L30 (−9.8%), ~$18,348 last 3 months, ~$53,887 last 6 months, last 12 months and all-time ~$87,381. Asking price $70,000. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~06:22 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Aggregate one high-intent paid opportunity stream (studies, grants, RFPs, clinical trials) and charge a monthly filter fee.
companies.whyItPrints: People pay for a cleaner list of paid research gigs. A directory with a subscription, which still works when finding the gigs is painful.

companies.name: Christian Tech Jobs
companies.description: Job board for curated tech roles at Christian companies, nonprofits, startups, and churches (the value proposition on TrustMRR). ~45,600 users (founder-stated). Founded Oct 2023, US. The short TrustMRR description field still says blockchain/DeFi. That looks like a stale blurb. The insights text describes the Christian-organisation board, which matches the domain.
companies.evidence: ~$2,211 MRR, 284 active subscriptions, ~$3,939 L30 (+3.5%), ~$11,925 last 3 months, ~$21,622 last 6 months, ~$33,150 last 12 months, ~$39,597 all-time. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~06:07 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One identity, industry, or geography job board. Sell employer seats and featured listings.
companies.whyItPrints: Niche job boards are a forever business. Employers pay to post. Candidates show up for a filter that matches who they are. Low product surface.

companies.name: QuizWhizzer
companies.description: Game-based quizzes for classrooms. The founder says it has mostly been in maintenance mode, still gets 300 to 700 organic signups a day, and about 450,000 users (founder-stated). Pricing (company-stated): free forever, Pro $39 a year. Founded Oct 2019, UK. Listed for sale at $30,000, about 1.6× (TrustMRR). L30 profit margin 40% (TrustMRR snapshot).
companies.evidence: ~$739 MRR, 206 active subscriptions, ~$1,597 L30 (+27.7%), ~$3,488 last 3 months, ~$5,474 last 6 months, ~$12,261 last 12 months, ~$123,200 all-time. Asking price $30,000. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~04:33 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: Ship a simple teacher tool, ride search for a decade, sell when you are bored. An annual Pro keeps renewals calm.
companies.whyItPrints: A classroom quiz tool that kept collecting annual Pro plans without a growth team. Maintenance mode plus search traffic is the quiet exit.

companies.name: Wawp
companies.description: WhatsApp automation for WooCommerce: cart recovery, cash-on-delivery anti-fraud OTP, multi-agent support, and a developer REST API (company-stated). Aimed at high cash-on-delivery merchants and stores that hate Meta setup friction and per-message fees (company-stated). Free to start, Pro for the paid tier (company-stated). ~12,560 users (founder-stated). Founded May 2022, Egypt. L30 profit margin 82% (TrustMRR snapshot).
companies.evidence: Stripe and Dodo. ~$324 MRR, 28 active subscriptions, ~$1,087 L30 (−28.9%), ~$2,615 last 3 months, ~$8,490 last 6 months, ~$23,628 last 12 months, ~$58,672 all-time. Last 30 days are soft against the last year. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~04:33 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One commerce platform, one chat channel, one regional pain (cash-on-delivery fraud, cart recovery, a one-time code). Sell a plugin.
companies.whyItPrints: WooCommerce stores in cash-on-delivery markets lose money to fake orders and abandoned carts. WhatsApp is the channel. This is the glue.

companies.name: Mittral
companies.description: Purchase request, approval chain, and purchase-order PDF software for small businesses (company-stated). Replaces asking in email, a manager saying fine from their phone, and a purchase order typed later. Pricing (company-stated): free forever for small teams, then roughly $39, $128, $227, or $550 a month as seats grow. Founded Nov 2023, UK.
companies.evidence: ~$151 MRR, 3 active subscriptions, ~$152 L30, ~$512 last 3 months, ~$1,026 last 6 months, ~$2,595 last 12 months, ~$25,246 all-time. Early traction. Included for the lane, not the headline. Revenue synced Oct 15, 2026 ~08:27 Warsaw.
companies.indieAngle: One approval workflow small businesses still run in Gmail. Charge per seat. Export PDFs an accountant will trust.
companies.whyItPrints: Procurement is painful and full of audit trails. Small today. The category is not going away.
